doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

title: Faith and generosity
summary: May says his faith brings thankfulness, giving, and seeing people as related.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Does your faith have anything to do with your music.

Oh yes, oh yes. I feel honestly, I feel I’m always very thankful and I just try to send that out as much as I possibly can. Because for me to have two dollars in my pocket and the desire to give away fifty cents of it to somebody, for doing something for me or whatever, I mean I feel that that’s what we’re here for. We’re all related. You might not like me but I’m still related to you. And I think we’re all here to help one another, to make life easier for each other. I mean if you have that kind of attitude, to me it seems
like it’s easier to smile — you know, somebody steps on your toe “oh, did I hurt you?” You know than to fight with them or something.
Yeah, I agree. It takes more energy to be nasty.
Yeah. And you can live a lot longer if you see the glass if half full, it’s much better I think.
